_comment: DEPLOYMENT CONFIG. One place for the facts a build needs but a designer
cannot invent. Everything domain-dependent — canonical, og:url, hreflang,
sitemap.xml, the robots Sitemap line and the analytics domain — is generated
from `url`, and is SKIPPED while it is empty rather than emitted with a
placeholder. A wrong canonical is worse than a missing one: it tells search
engines the real page lives somewhere else.
`hsts` STAYS FALSE until check 4 in docs/44-launch.md §2 shows the live site
serving TLS and its headers. The header is cached by browsers for a year:
switch it on over a host that cannot serve https and visitors are locked out
of the site, not merely inconvenienced. Once verified, set it to true and
run `node build.js` — one field, not a hand-edited server file.
MOVING DOMAIN (to pixora.net or anything else) is this one field plus
`node build.js`. Nothing else in the repository names a host. The rest of
the move — 301s from the old host, renaming the site in Plausible, Search
Console's change of address — is in docs/44-launch.md §3.
NOTE the review surface: GitHub Pages serves the modular source and ignores
.htaccess, so no CSP, no rewrites and no custom 404 there. It is for reading
the pages, not for judging the deployment.

contact._comment: WhatsApp number in wa.me form (digits only, country code first). One place: build-pricing.js renders every package CTA from it.

_comment: ANALYTICS. Off until a provider is named here — choosing who receives a
visitor's data is not a default a build script should pick. Set `provider`
to "plausible" (or "umami") and fill in the fields below; build-deploy.js
then adds the provider's script to the deployed pages, and src/scripts/
analytics.js starts reporting the four events it already collects.
Both options are cookieless and send no personal data, which is why they
need no consent banner under most readings — but a privacy policy naming
the provider must ship in the same release.
Note the trade: this is the only third-party request the site makes. The
zero-request property is spent deliberately, on the one thing the project
cannot proceed without.
